raw.reasoning:
The user wants me to refine the translation of a Tanach verse. Let me analyze:

Verse: וַיִּֽהְי֤וּ שְׁנֵיהֶם֙ עֲרוּמִּ֔ים הָֽאָדָ֖ם וְאִשְׁתּ֑וֹ וְלֹ֖א יִתְבּשָֽׁשׁוּ:

This is from Genesis 2:25. Let me parse it:
- וַיִּֽהְי֤וּ = "and they were"
- שְׁנֵיהֶם֙ = "the two of them"
- עֲרוּמִּ֔ים = "naked" (but this word also has connotations of being "clever/crafty" in other contexts - from the root ע.ר.מ)
- הָֽאָדָ֖ם = "the man"
- וְאִשְׁתּ֑וֹ = "and his wife"
- וְלֹ֖א = "and not"
- יִתְבּשָֽׁשׁוּ = "they were ashamed" (niphal imperfect)

The existing translation says: "Now they were both naked, the man and his wife, but they were not ashamed."

The Hebrew word עֲרוּמִּים is interesting - it comes from the root ע.ר.מ which in qal can mean "to be naked" but also "to be clever/shrewd." In this context, it's clearly "naked" (as in unclothed).

The word יִתְבּשָֽׁשׁוּ is from the root ב.ש.ש and means "to be ashamed."


My refined translation: "Now both of them were naked, the man and his wife, and they were not ashamed."

The adjustment here is more natural English phrasing—"both of them were naked" flows better than the more literal "they were both naked," and the repetition of "and" maintains the parallel structure of the Hebrew more effectively.
